definitions.explanation: A thin, absorbent paper used for Japanese calligraphy (書道). Standard size is approximately 24cm × 33cm. Named because it is roughly half the size of a full sheet of traditional Japanese paper.

examples.english: To write on calligraphy paper with a brush.

examples.japanese: ⟦{書道|しょどう}→書道：04178_shodou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{半紙|はんし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: We use calligraphy paper in calligraphy class.

examples.japanese: {百均|ひゃっきん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{半紙|はんし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}って→買う：00489_kau⟧きた⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{墨|すみ}→墨：02155_sumi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{乗|の}り⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あまり→あまり：00604_amari⟧⟦{良|よ}くなかった→良い：02350_yoi⟧。
examples.english: I bought calligraphy paper at the hundred-yen store, but the ink didn't adhere very well.

notes:
USAGE:
Familiar to all Japanese people from ⟦{書道|しょどう}→書道：04178_shodou⟧ (calligraphy) classes in school. The paper is designed to absorb ink from a ⟦{筆|ふで}→筆：03601_fude⟧ (brush). Quality varies widely — practice paper is inexpensive, while high-quality {半紙|はんし} for exhibitions can be costly.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {半紙|はんし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧ (to write on calligraphy paper)
- {練習用|れんしゅうよう}{半紙|はんし} (practice calligraphy paper)
- {半紙|はんし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{広|ひろ}げる→広げる：01981_hirogeru⟧ (to spread out calligraphy paper)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{和紙|わし}→和紙：02268_washi⟧: Japanese paper — the broader category of traditional Japanese paper
- ⟦{画用紙|がようし}→画用紙：11511_gayoushi⟧: drawing paper — thicker paper for painting and drawing
